## University Courses

### [Applied Survival Analysis](https://lmaowisc.github.io/BMI741/) {#applied-survival-analysis}
:::: {.course-entry}
::: {.course-avatar}
[![Applied Survival Analysis course site](images/surv_hex.png)](https://lmaowisc.github.io/BMI741/){.course-image-link}\
[Spring 2020 -- 2025]{.course-date}
:::

::: {.course-outline}
Provides a survey of statistical methods for time-to-event data arising in medical and industrial settings.

-   Kaplan-Meier estimator, log-rank test, Cox proportional hazards model
-   Multiple failures, recurrent events, competing risks, joint analysis with longitudinal data, multistate processes, composite endpoints
-   Causal inference, machine learning

Emphasizes case studies and data analysis (using R)
:::
::::


### [Applied Longitudinal Analysis](https://lmaowisc.github.io/longitudinal-analysis/) {#applied-longitudinal-analysis}
:::: {.course-entry}
::: {.course-avatar}
[![Applied Longitudinal Analysis course site](images/longitudinal-course.svg)](https://lmaowisc.github.io/longitudinal-analysis/){.course-image-link}\
[Spring 2019]{.course-date}
:::

::: {.course-outline}
Introduces statistical methods for repeated measurements and correlated outcomes, with applications in the health and behavioral sciences.

-   Response profiles, mean and covariance structures
-   Linear mixed-effects models and growth curves
-   Marginal models, generalized estimating equations (GEE), and generalized linear mixed-effects models
-   Missing data, smoothing, and multilevel models

Includes 24 lectures, SAS examples, and datasets for practice
:::
::::


## Workshops

### [Tidy Survival Analysis: Applying R's Tidyverse to Survival Data](https://lmaowisc.github.io/tidysurv/) {#tidy-survival-analysis}
:::: {.course-entry}
::: {.course-avatar}
[![Tidy Survival Analysis workshop site](images/tidy-survival-workshop.svg)](https://lmaowisc.github.io/tidysurv/){.course-image-link}\
[JSM 2025]{.course-date}
:::

::: {.course-outline}
Develops a reproducible R workflow for preparing, analyzing, and visualizing survival data through five modules.

-   Survival concepts and censoring, illustrated with breast cancer data
-   Data preparation, follow-up plots, and descriptive tables with the Tidyverse
-   Survival curves and competing-risk estimates, with tables and graphics
-   Cox and Fine-Gray regression, model summaries, and diagnostics
-   Machine learning for survival outcomes with `tidymodels`

Emphasizes worked examples and consistent data workflows in R
:::
::::

### [Statistical Methods for Composite Endpoints: Win Ratio and Beyond](https://lmaowisc.github.io/ce/) {#composite-endpoints}
:::: {.course-entry}
::: {.course-avatar}
[![Statistical Methods for Composite Endpoints workshop site](images/composite-endpoints-workshop.svg)](https://lmaowisc.github.io/ce/){.course-image-link}\
[NESS 2025]{.course-date}
:::

::: {.course-outline}
Examines methods for combining outcomes in clinical trials, progressing from foundational concepts to estimation, regression, and open questions.

-   Composite endpoint choices, traditional approaches, and win ratio methods
-   Testing and sample size planning, including recurrent events
-   Restricted win ratio, average win time, and while-alive loss rate
-   Proportional win-fractions regression, diagnostics, and risk prediction
-   Further topics: covariate adjustment, interim monitoring, and meta-analysis

Includes practical R examples for analysis and interpretation
:::
::::
